claim: The canonical practitioner recipe for Glances-on-Proxmox (Derek Seaman, Apr 2023, updated Feb 2026 for Proxmox 8.x/9.x) requires: pipx install 'glances[all]', a symlink into /usr/local/bin, interactive credential setup, loading the drivetemp kernel module for SATA temps, and a hand-written systemd unit — a multi-step per-host procedure
stance_target: per-host deployment burden of the incumbent Python-webserver pattern is real and documented; a single static NixOS module for the fleet eliminates it
scope_conditions: Proxmox VE 8.x/9.x hosts (Debian bookworm/trixie base); Glances via pipx; systemd service
quoted_support: apt-get install pipx ... pipx install 'glances[all]' ... echo "drivetemp" >> /etc/modules ... nano /etc/systemd/system/glances.service ... systemctl enable glances.service

claim: Proxmox VE 8 upgrades silently killed existing Glances installs and required full reinstalls — the PVE8/Debian bookworm transition initially broke Glances entirely, fixed only via community-provided workarounds (tteck)
stance_target: OS upgrades breaking per-host Python telemetry installs is a concrete fleet failure mode; declarative NixOS packaging with pinned builds survives system upgrades
scope_conditions: Proxmox VE 8.0 on Debian bookworm, mid-2023
quoted_support: Proxmox VE 8.0 is based on Debian bookworm, which initially causes a python compatibility issue with Glances. However, thanks to tteck, he provided a solution which I've incorporated into this guide. If you upgrade to Proxmox VE 8.0, and had Glances working on a prior version you will need to re-install.

claim: PEP 668 'externally-managed-environment' blocks system-wide pip installs of Glances on Debian bookworm — commenters resorted to venvs, pipx, or the dangerous 'rm -rf /usr/lib/python3.*/EXTERNALLY-MANAGED' workaround
stance_target: packaging Python telemetry onto modern hosts is an actively painful, failure-prone step that a static Rust binary sidesteps entirely
quoted_support: The install command runs and gives me this at the end: error: externally-managed-environment × This environment is externally managed ... I found several warnings against that step. Here is an alternative that seems to work for me: apt-get install pipx ... pipx install 'glances[all]'

claim: Omitting the '-u username' flag from the Glances systemd ExecStart line silently ignored credentials and exposed the webserver to anonymous users — a security footgun corrected in the guide after reader reports
stance_target: per-host credential wiring is error-prone; auth misconfiguration silently degrades to open exposure — an agent with a single config path and no per-host webserver avoids this class
scope_conditions: Glances systemd service on Proxmox; reader-reported
quoted_support: I had to use /usr/local/bin/glances -w -u HERE-MY-GLANCES-USERNAME as the ExecStart command in /etc/systemd/system/glances.service or else it ignored the credentials and made the info accessible for anonymous users

claim: Glances service startup can hang on hostname resolution, requiring '--disable-autodiscover' in the ExecStart to start reliably as a service
stance_target: the incumbent's startup path contains nondeterministic network-dependent hangs — a known unreliability class for fleet agents
scope_conditions: Glances systemd service, Proxmox host, reader-reported
quoted_support: I ran into some extra fun with glances failing to start (as a service) due to a know issue with resolving the host name. Changing the config file to disable autodiscover fixed it: ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/glances -w -u root --disable-autodiscover

claim: Glances CPU temperature disagreed with lm-sensors by roughly 17°C on the same i7-1255U host (lm-sensors Package id 0: +36.0°C vs Glances ~53°C), with no resolution offered in the thread
stance_target: metric fidelity of the incumbent is questionable; an agent should read sensors via a documented canonical path (sysfs/hwmon) and validate against lm-sensors
scope_conditions: Intel i7-1255U host; Glances vs lm-sensors, reader-reported
quoted_support: I noticed the CPU temps I get when running lm-sensors are different than what's reported in Glances. lm-sensors says Package id 0: +36.0°C whereas Glances says 127 F (so around 53 C).

claim: The guide's HA integration setup requires manually entering the Proxmox host IP plus username/password per host in the HA UI — each additional monitored Proxmox host means repeating the whole per-host installation and config-entry process
stance_target: fleet scaling of the incumbent is linear manual work per host; declarative per-host modules plus MQTT auto-discovery make new hosts appear without HA-side configuration
scope_conditions: Home Assistant Glances integration; multiple Proxmox hosts
quoted_support: Yes, the add-on can monitor multiple servers. Just repeat the add-on process and use the IP of the second proxmox server.
